subject.title: improve: reduce GPT-5.6 coding harness overhead

question: Does the retained compact execution and code-mode wording preserve the intended model-facing approval and elevated-access safety contract well enough to accept the prompt-size tradeoff?
rationale: This is a user-facing agent-behavior and security-boundary judgment; tests can assert selected phrases but cannot fully establish how the compressed contract affects real coding-model tool use.

options.title: Require proof and security review
options.body: Request redacted live output for the parity run plus a focused review of direct and code-mode approval semantics before merge.

options.title: Accept the compact contract
options.body: Merge after explicitly accepting that runtime enforcement, rather than fuller model-facing guidance, is the primary safety control.

options.title: Narrow the change
options.body: Land timing reporting separately and defer prompt compression until the model-facing security contract has dedicated evidence.

recommendation.title: Require proof and security review
recommendation.body: Request redacted live output for the parity run plus a focused review of direct and code-mode approval semantics before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history ties this contributor to both changed prompt contracts and the parity-report work, though broader ownership evidence is limited.
